question: Why must you pass &age (the address of age) rather than just age to scanf("%d", ...) when reading an integer?
options: It's just a stylistic convention with no real effect
scanf() only accepts pointers to strings
Passing age would cause a compile error
scanf() needs the memory address of the variable so it can write the input value directly into it
explanation: C passes arguments by value, so scanf() needs a pointer (the variable's address, &age) in order to modify age's actual storage location with the value read from input.
